title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation (manuscript pp. 293-650) of La Longue Marche (1981). Pi^_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It is free profinite on two generators, with standard loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity satisfying l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1.

The symmetries in play:
- sigma_infinity is an involution (a reflection or complex-conjugation type symmetry fixing infinity, with sigma_0, sigma_1 its conjugates).
- rho is the order-3 rotation of the three points.
- eps_0 = sigma_infinity rho and eps_1 = rho sigma_infinity are 'half-loops', with eps_i^2 = l_i.
- G^+_{0,3} is an enlarged group containing Pi^_{0,3} together with these symmetries, and phi^ : Pi^_{0,3} -> G^+_{0,3} is a 'presumptive' homomorphism defined by formula (18).

On this page Grothendieck summarizes the computation of p.61 as a Proposition.

Setting. An outer action on Pi^_{0,3} is given by explicit formulas (11). It is parametrized by:
- g_0 in Pi^_{0,3}, determined up to a power of l_0;
- an exponent p in Z^* (cyclotomic-character-like);
- gamma in Z^*, uniquely determined by g_0 and p.
The action is required to commute with sigma_infinity, which imposes conditions (9) and (10) on the data. These look like the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (S_3-symmetry) relations familiar from Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory. Generation conditions (11 bis) are added.

Claim. The outer homomorphism phi^ commutes with the given outer action if and only if there is beta in Z^ such that (24) holds:
 eps_1^{-beta} h_0 eps_0^{beta} = sigma_infinity(phi^(h_0))^{-1} phi^(h_0),
where h_0 = g_0^{-1} sigma_infinity(g_0).

Equivalently, writing mu~ = [sigma_infinity, mu], this is (27):
 eps_1^{-beta} g_0~ eps_0^{beta} = (phi^(g_0~))~,
which is a twisted equivariance of phi^ with respect to the commutator-with-sigma_infinity map.

For fixed beta it is also equivalent to:
- the compatibility (20) evaluated on x = l_infinity, i.e.
- (28): u(l'_infinity) = int(lambda^{-1} phi^(g_infinity))(l'_infinity^beta),
- with (29): g_infinity = g_0 l_0^{-gamma} rho^{-1}(h_0), and lambda given by (22).

Why only l_infinity matters. Compatibility on l_0 holds by construction, and compatibility on l_1 follows by sigma_infinity-symmetry (p.61, formula (23)). So only the third loop gives a genuine condition. The free exponent beta records the ambiguity in choosing conjugating elements for an outer (rather than actual) action.

On p.61, replacing g_0 by g_0 eps_0^lambda changes beta to beta - 2 lambda, so only the parity of beta matters. On p.63 the condition is rewritten as (30) in terms of alpha = beta + gamma and p mod 3. Grothendieck then suspects the condition is 'not always fulfilled' and says the extra conditions of §39 should be made explicit in terms of g_0 and p.

Purpose. This is a step in determining which GT-like outer actions on pi_1(P^1 - 3 points), compatible with the S_3 and real-structure symmetries, are compatible with an auxiliary homomorphism phi^. The aim is to cut out a combinatorial candidate for the image of Gal(Q-bar/Q).
errors: The l_0 and l_1 cases are not re-checked on this page. Reducing commutation of an outer homomorphism to a single generator (l_infinity) needs the conjugating elements chosen for l_0, l_1, l_infinity to be coherent. The parameter beta is meant to absorb this, but coherence is asserted rather than verified here.

Grothendieck himself on p.63 suspects the resulting condition is not automatically satisfied. So the Proposition is an equivalence, not an existence result; whether the condition holds for actual Galois actions is left open.
The notation clash between rho as the rotation and the exponent p in Z^* is easy to misread; the transcription conflates them.

ideas.what: Parametrization of outer actions on the profinite free group Pi^_{0,3} by data (g_0, p, gamma), subject to symmetry relations (9), (10) coming from S_3 and the involution sigma_infinity
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck-Teichmüller-type parametrization (lambda, f) with 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations; GT^ and its variants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Grothendieck's motivation in Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (circulated); this explicit form unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility of the outer action with phi^ : Pi^_{0,3} -> G^+_{0,3} is equivalent to a twisted commutator identity eps_1^{-beta} [sigma_infinity, g_0] eps_0^{beta} = [sigma_infinity, phi^([sigma_infinity, g_0])] for some beta in Z^
ideas.modern_name: Equivariance condition for a GT-like action with respect to the real structure (complex conjugation) and half-loops
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related considerations of complex conjugation in GT: Ihara, Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura; no exact counterpart known

ideas.what: Use of half-loops eps_i = sigma rho (with eps_i^2 = l_i) in the dihedral/S_3-extended group, and the parity reduction of beta under g_0 -> g_0 eps_0^lambda
ideas.modern_name: Extension of pi_1 by real-structure involutions (orbifold/real fundamental group); dihedral symmetries of P^1 minus 3 points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; real-structure versions of GT were treated later by several authors

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives a precise necessary and sufficient condition (24)/(27)/(30) for his presumptive homomorphism phi^ to commute with a GT-type outer action. On p.63 he suspects it is not always satisfied, and leaves open making the §39 conditions explicit in g_0 and p. Whether this condition is implied by the Drinfeld relations, or is an extra constraint cutting GT^ down, appears not to have been studied.
missed.quote: il faut et il suffit que l'on puisse trouver un beta in Z^, tel que l'on ait (24), ou ce qui revient au même, (27).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Additional symmetry constraints on GT^ that hold for Gal(Q-bar/Q) are of continuing interest (cf. Lochak-Schneps conditions, the question GT^ = G_Q?). A real-structure constraint of this form might either be a consequence of the known relations or a new one.

missed.claim: Real structure (the involution sigma_infinity, i.e. complex conjugation) is built into the definition of the parametrizing data and the compatibility equations from the start, roughly a decade before published GT theory systematically treated complex conjugation.
missed.quote: en termes d'une action effective ... qui commute à sigma_infinity
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links the dihedral/real-orbifold fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points with GT-type equations; it could inform work on real versions of GT and on the image of complex conjugation.

deep.surprise_reason: It is a concrete, unpublished intermediate result in Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld exploration of GT-like equations, incorporating real structure. The general direction is known to specialists, but this specific equivalence and its open status are not in the literature. Its exact relation to modern GT conditions cannot be pinned down from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: (29) should read g_infinity = g_0 l_0^{-gamma} rho^{-1}(h_0), not rho^{-1}(l_0); this is consistent with p.63.
'cette action à vérifier les conditions' is better read as '[les données g_0, p (et gamma)] étant donc assujetties à vérifier les conditions (9) et (10)'.
The exponent parameter written 'rho in Z^*' is most likely 'p in Z^*' (cf. p.63, 'la valeur de p in Z^* mod 3'), distinct from the rotation rho.
The insertion above 'g_0 in Pi^_{0,3}' is plausibly 'mod l_0' or '(défini à une puissance de l_0 près)', i.e. g_0 determined up to l_0-powers; uncertain.
'une action ext. ne des groupes à lacets' is probably 'une action extérieure ... sur le groupe à lacets Pi^_{0,3}'.
Margin note reads 'variante : 24 bis', referring to the alternative form (24 bis) on p.61.
